label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Original Revision practice. In an activity-on-arrow network, A (2 days) precedes parallel B (4 days) and C (3 days). Activity D (2 days) may start only when BOTH B and C finish. A zero-duration dummy preserves the dependency.
question.stem: Which pair correctly identifies the project duration and critical path?

option_rationale: A is incorrect because the A–C–D route is 7 days, but the other required route takes longer.
B is correct because A–B–D takes 2+4+2 = 8 days, longer than A–C–dummy–D at 7 days.
C is incorrect because the original C branch takes 3 days, not 5.
D is incorrect because B and C run in parallel after A; both routes include A.
mark_scheme.model_answer: B. A–B–D takes 8 days; the parallel route A–C–dummy–D takes 7 days. The 8-day route determines the earliest project completion.
